title: Above the Rooftops
story:
The Great Clockwork hummed with steady precision, its iron pendulum sweeping through the loft in long, solemn arcs. Barnaby wiped a trace of machine oil from his thumb onto a rag and smiled down at James, gesturing toward a narrow arched doorway tucked behind the counterweights. With a gentle click of the iron latch, this man pushed the door outward, letting a sudden rush of cool mountain wind sweep across the dusty floorboards.

James followed him out onto the stone balcony that wrapped around the library's clock tower, high above Oakhaven. The entire world opened before them beneath the soft gray bell of the highland sky. There was Weaver's Wharf, no larger than a handful of scattered wooden blocks along the water. There was the Plaza of the Fountain, where townsfolk bustled beneath rain-spotted canvas awnings. There was the green slope of the Terrace Gardens, where Pippin had chased pinecones only yesterday.

Beside him, Barnaby rested his hands against the weathered stone balustrade, gazing past the perimeter of the town toward the blue, mist-wreathed ridges that rose into the southern clouds. The air up here smelled different than the library below—it smelled of rain-washed slate, chimney smoke, and the deep, damp greenery of forests far beyond the valley.

James touched the new five-toothed brass cog nestled against his strap, watching a swallow dart beneath the copper eaves. Looking toward the vast and unfamiliar mountains on the horizon, he whispered his quiet greeting into the breeze: 'Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next.' Behind them, the great bells of the tower stirred, sending a deep, resonant pulse trembling through the very stones under their feet.
location: The Clock Tower Balcony, Grand Library, Oakhaven
